title: Soil pedostructure-based method for calculating the soil-water holding properties
author: Assi, Mohtar, et al.
materials: This work builds on the work of Assi et al. [3] and Braudeau et al. [2] to develop a methodology for calculating the FC, PWP, and AW.

steps.title: Collect soil cores
steps.instruction: Using standard cylindrical stainless‑steel soil cores (diameter Φ = 5 cm, height h = 5 cm) collect one core from the top horizon of each of the two target soils: (1) Chazos loamy fine‑sand Alfisol (4 % clay, 13 % silt, 83 % sand) from College Station, TX, USA; (2) Sabkha silt‑loam Aridisol (15 % clay, 65 % silt, 20 % sand) from Al Khor, Qatar.

steps.title: Prepare samples for TypoSoil™
steps.instruction: Follow the TypoSoil™ user manual to condition each core for measurement (e.g., ensure the core fits the instrument, label, and keep at ambient conditions). If the water retention curve (WRC) and shrinkage curve (ShC) have already been measured with another apparatus, skip to step 4.

steps.title: Measure state variables with TypoSoil™
steps.instruction: Place up to eight prepared cores in the TypoSoil™ chamber (Fig. 2a). The device records simultaneously: • moisture content by balance “MASSE”; • soil suction by ceramic‑cup tensiometer “TENSIO”; • specific volume by two laser beams “BARR 1”, “BARR 2” and one laser spot “SPOT”. Record the raw data for each run as shown in Table 1.

substeps.instruction: Slot 2 Code RR LOC2 UDDate 25/7/2013 – 8 h 31 Batch TYPO130725 Operator Josh GenDate 20130728‑093755

steps.title: Calculate water content and specific volume

substeps.instruction: Water content (W, kg water kg⁻¹ solid) using Equation (1): W = (m − Ms) / Ms, where m is the measured mass (kg water) and Ms is the dry mass obtained after oven‑drying at 105 °C.
Specific volume (V¯, dm³ kg⁻¹ solid) using Equation (2): V¯ = π D² H / (4 Ms) × 10⁻⁴, where D and H are the laser‑measured diameter and height (dm).

steps.title: Construct WRC and ShC
steps.instruction: Plot the calculated water content (W) against:

substeps.instruction: Soil suction (h, dm ≈ kPa) to obtain the water retention curve (WRC).
Specific volume (V¯, dm³ kg⁻¹ solid) to obtain the soil shrinkage curve (ShC).

steps.title: Extract pedostructure parameters
steps.instruction: Fit the thermodynamic equations described in Assi et al. [3] and Braudeau et al. [4] to the measured WRC and ShC to obtain the characteristic parameters (e.g., WM, WC, WB, WN, WA, WD, WE, WL, WF, Ēma, Ēmi, kN, kL, etc.).

steps.title: Compute pedostructure water contents
steps.instruction: Using the extracted parameters, calculate the following water‑content pools with the equations provided in the manuscript:

substeps.instruction: Inter‑pedal water (w_ip) – Eq. (3): w_ip = (1 / kL) · ln[1 + exp(kL·(W − WL))]
Macro‑pore water (W_ma_eq) – Eq. (4): W_ma_eq = [W + Ē_A + W + Ē_A² − 4 Ē_ma A_W] / 2
Micro‑pore water (W_mi_eq) – Eq. (5): W_mi_eq = W − W_ma_eq = W − Ē_A − [W + Ē_A² − 4 Ē_ma A_W] / 2
Basic water (w_bs) – Eq. (6): w_bs = (1 / kN) · ln[1 + exp(kN·(W − W_mi_eq))]
Residual water (w_re) – Eq. (7): w_re = W − (1 / kN) · ln[1 + exp(kN·(W − W_mi_eq))]

steps.title: Calculate field capacity, wilting point, and available water
steps.instruction: Enter the extracted parameters and the equations above into the supplied Excel spreadsheets (provided as supplementary material). The spreadsheets output the field capacity (FC), permanent wilting point (PWP), and available water (AW) for each soil.

steps.title: Reference variable definitions (Table 2)
steps.instruction: Consult Table 2 for the meaning, units, and symbols of all variables used in the calculations (e.g., WSat, Wma, Wmi, E¯ma, E¯mi, kN, kL, etc.).
